scope: Recent Stage 000 retry/hold history in /work/saivage-v3/.saivage/plan-history.json and stage summaries for retries/holds 15-18; no secrets/provider configs/opt/service controls/unauthorized paths read.
executive_summary: Stage 000 is blocked by an operator-owned runtime prerequisite: repeated fresh retries 15, 16, 17, and 18 all record active Node v24.15.0 while both root and web package.json require >=22.12.0 <23. Within planner/manager scope, no corrective action remains other than preserving the archived escalation/hold evidence and waiting for explicit operator evidence that Node was fixed; continuing immediate fresh retries without such evidence is repeated probing and contradicts the no-probe hold intent.

questions_answered.question: 1. Given repeated fresh retries observing Node v24.15.0 outside required >=22.12.0 <23, is there any planner/manager-scope corrective action remaining besides documenting hold and waiting for operator environment change?
questions_answered.answer: No. The summaries and prerequisite artifacts consistently classify the blocker as operator-owned and explicitly prohibit manager/coder repair actions such as Node switching, dependency install, service/LXC control, or environment repair. Stage managers correctly stopped before validation because the project engine constraint is unsatisfied. The only in-scope next action before Node is fixed is documentation/hold state maintenance; at the plan-state level even additional no-probe hold stages are redundant once the hold is archived and current plan has no pending stage.

questions_answered.question: 2. Does continuously queuing and dispatching immediate fresh retry stages violate the stated no repeated probing / operator hold intent when no evidence says Node was fixed?
questions_answered.answer: Yes. Hold artifacts 16 and 17 state that holds must use prior evidence only and that no fresh Node/npm/jq/git/environment probe should run until the operator provides active Node >=22.12.0 <23. Despite that, history shows immediate fresh retries 16, 17, and 18 after hold entries, each probing Node and rediscovering v24.15.0. That pattern is inconsistent with the explicit no-probe operator hold intent unless there is intervening operator evidence of a runtime fix; no such evidence appears in the inspected history.

questions_answered.question: 3. What plan state best represents a blocked operator hold without causing automatic retry loops: an active pending fresh retry, an active no-probe hold, or no pending stage with archived escalation and explicit operator-required action?
questions_answered.answer: The best state is no pending stage with archived escalation/hold evidence and an explicit operator-required action. The current /work/saivage-v3/.saivage/plan.json already has current_stage_id null and an empty stages array, which accurately prevents automatic manager dispatch and retry loops. An active pending fresh retry causes probes; an active no-probe hold can still be repeatedly dispatched/escalated as seen in hold 16/17 and does not add new information after the hold artifact exists.

questions_answered.question: 4. When Node is eventually fixed by the operator, what exact next stage should be seeded?
questions_answered.answer: Seed a new fresh Stage 000 prerequisite retry stage, not Stage 001. The concrete id should follow the existing retry naming/numbering convention as the next unused retry: 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-19. That stage should freshly verify Node >=22.12.0 <23 and all Stage 000 prerequisites before any validation/baseline work. Only after Stage 000 closes successfully should normal advancement pick the first published unrecorded stage, currently 001-real-llm-analyst-resolver.

findings.title: Repeated immediate fresh retries conflict with no-probe operator hold intent absent evidence of Node repair
evidence: .saivage/stages/000-breakage-detection-harness-node-runtime-hold-16/hold.json has evidence_mode prior-summary-only, prohibited_actions.runtime_probe_attempted false, and next_action requiring operator Node >=22.12.0 <23 then a fresh retry.

.saivage/stages/000-breakage-detection-harness-node-runtime-hold-17/no-probe-operator-hold.json has evidence_source_mode stating no fresh environment/git/Node/npm/jq/validation/repair probe was run for the hold task, and next_actionable_step requiring operator-provided Node >=22.12.0 <23 followed by a fresh retry.
History tail shows the loop: fresh retry 16 -> hold 16 -> fresh retry 17 -> hold 17 -> fresh retry 18, all escalated; no inspected entry records operator-provided Node fix evidence between them.
Fresh retry 18 summary states the Manager performed a direct non-mutating prerequisite probe and again observed Node v24.15.0.
findings.root_cause: The planner loop appears to treat escalated hold/fresh-retry stages as a reason to enqueue another immediate fresh retry, instead of quiescing until an external operator action is recorded.
findings.impact: Consumes agents, repeats the same environment probe, creates noisy history, and risks violating the explicit operator-hold/no-repeated-probing instruction. It does not move Stage 000 closer to acceptance because the blocker is outside Saivage manager/coder authority.

findings.title: Current empty plan state is the correct blocked-hold representation
evidence: .saivage/plan.json lines 2-4 show updated_at 2026-05-25T03:26:07.980Z, current_stage_id null, and stages [].
The plan-history tail contains archived escalations/holds through 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-18.
No pending stage means the manager will not automatically dispatch another fresh probe or no-probe hold stage.
findings.root_cause: A blocked operator prerequisite is not an executable project stage until the operator changes the environment or supplies evidence that the runtime was fixed.
findings.impact: Maintaining current_stage_id null and stages [] prevents retry loops while preserving the archived evidence needed for Chat/Planner/operator status reporting.

findings.title: After operator Node fix, the next executable stage is a new fresh Stage 000 retry, not Stage 001
evidence: Published stage directories are 000-breakage-detection-harness, 001-real-llm-analyst-resolver, and 002-tool-surface-alignment; the first published unrecorded stage is 001-real-llm-analyst-resolver, but Stage 000 remains incomplete in the retry/hold summaries.
Hold 16 and hold 17 artifacts both state that after operator provides Node >=22.12.0 <23, Stage 000 must run a fresh prerequisite retry before validation or baseline work.
Existing retry IDs use the convention 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-N, with N=18 most recent; the next unused retry id is N=19.
findings.root_cause: Stage advancement rules apply after the current stage closes; Stage 000 has not closed because validation was never allowed to run under the wrong Node runtime.
findings.impact: Seeding Stage 001 immediately after Node repair would skip the required Stage 000 acceptance gate. Seeding 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-19 preserves stage order and rechecks all prerequisites against the fixed runtime.

recommendations.action: Keep /work/saivage-v3/.saivage/plan.json with current_stage_id null and stages [] while Node remains unfixed; do not seed additional fresh retry or no-probe hold stages unless explicit operator evidence says Node >=22.12.0 <23 is active.

Operator-facing status references the archived hold/escalation artifacts and states the required external action: activate Node >=22.12.0 <23 for /work/saivage-v3.

recommendations.action: When the operator confirms/fixes Node, seed current_stage_id and stages with the next fresh retry id: 000-breakage-detection-harness-fresh-retry-after-node-runtime-fixed-19.
acceptance_criteria: The fresh retry first runs a read-only prerequisite probe verifying Node satisfies >=22.12.0 <23 from /work/saivage-v3.
If prerequisites are green, continue Stage 000 plan validation exactly as published; if Node is still out of range, escalate once and return to no-pending-stage hold state.

recommendations.action: Update planner retry policy/state machine so an escalation classified as operator-runtime-prerequisite hold is terminal/quiescent until an external operator-fix signal is present, rather than automatically enqueueing another immediate retry.

For external-operator blockers, Planner archives the escalation and emits an operator-required action without setting a pending stage.
A fresh retry is only seeded after a distinct operator-fix event/evidence is recorded.
